sections.html:
Walker County fills Georgia's northwest corner, right against the Tennessee line, and its northern end belongs to the Chattanooga commuting zone. LaFayette is the county seat. At 447 square miles it holds ridges, caves and coves rather than flat farmland, so one seller may list a lot in town while the next has a mountainside tract or acreage in a valley, and the tax picture differs for each. About 51% of residents lived in rural areas at the last census.

Five incorporated cities sit inside the county: Chickamauga, LaFayette, Lookout Mountain, Rossville and a small piece of Fort Oglethorpe. The Walker County School District covers most of the county, while Chickamauga has its own city system, so check which district applies when you read a bill.

Walker County leans heavily toward homeowners, and prices run under the national figure. The population was 67,654 on census day in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 70,250.

In 2020, 28.2% of occupied homes were rented and 10.1% of all units stood empty.

Billing sits with the Tax Commissioner and valuation sits with the Board of Tax Assessors. The commissioner's office neither determines property value nor sets the tax rate.

  • Rock Spring: 122 Highway 95, mail to P O Box 510, Rock Spring, GA 30739, phone 706-638-2929, weekdays 8:00 A.M. until 4:30 P.M., with a drop box beside the front entrance.
  • Rossville: 2012 McFarland Gap Road in the Fairview community, same phone and hours.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: 706-638-4823, also the number for preferential assessment questions.
  • Search and pay online at walkercountytax.com.

Both counters take payments and questions, so use whichever is closer. Ask either one to walk you through the county and school levy lines on the bill.

Notices carry a 60-day window, which works out to December 20 in most years. If your printed bill shows another day, follow the bill. A mailed check needs a USPS postmark, not a meter stamp, and interest waits until 60 days past the bill's postmark.

  • Manufactured homes located in the county on January 1 are due April 1 each year and carry a 10% penalty plus 1% monthly interest when late, with a possible State Court citation.
  • The value date is January 1, so anyone who closes on a purchase after that date should confirm that the bill reaches them.

Your written appeal has to be in the assessors' hands by the 45th day after the notice date. Only three complaints count: taxability, value and uniformity. Disliking the size of the bill is not one of them.

After the assessors' own review, you may take the case to the Board of Equalization or to arbitration, and Superior Court sits beyond that. An owner who disagrees with the carried-forward value can also file a new return between January 1 and April 1. Taxable assessed value is 40% of market value under O.C.G.A. 48-5-7.

The local homestead amount applies whenever it is larger than the state one. Bring the warranty deed if this is your first application.

  • Standard homestead: $2,000 for state, school and county purposes.
  • Local senior exemptions begin at age 70: county tax with a $15,000 adjusted gross income limit, and county school tax with $50,000 off taxable value. A county school exemption at age 75 carries the same $15,000 limit.
  • Disabled veteran and armed forces surviving spouse exemptions: $81,080.
  • Tax deferral: ages 62 and up with gross household income of $15,000 or less, until a change of ownership or until deferred tax plus interest reaches 85% of market value.
  • Homeowner Tax Relief Grant: lowers assessed value by $18,000 for credit purposes and shows on the 2026 bill if a homestead exemption was on file by the April 1 cutoff. Rentals and investment property do not receive it.

A form that comes in after April 1 counts from the next tax year. Once approved, the exemption rolls forward on its own until the deed or your residence changes.

Ask the commissioner for the balance in writing, then let the closing agent send it out of your sale proceeds. Land with unpaid tax can be levied and sold, so clear every year before the keys change hands.

Treat a manufactured home on the land as its own account, because its tax runs on the April 1 calendar and not the autumn one. Inherited houses and rentals can have more than one tax year open, so request the status of each.

Here is how the sequence usually runs. Ask the commissioner for the balance on each parcel and each manufactured home. Confirm with the assessors that your exemptions are in place. Give the written figures to the closing agent, who pays the county first and sends you the rest. A cash sale to a buyer who takes the house as it stands can follow the same steps without a repair list, which suits hillside cabins and older town houses that would not pass a lender's inspection.

sections.h2: A walk through the courthouse steps
sections.html:
Two counters serve the whole county, so a visit rarely takes long. Rock Spring has the drop box by the front door if you would rather leave a payment than wait in line. Rossville in the Fairview community handles the same business for owners at the north end.

Bring the parcel number or the name on the bill, plus your warranty deed if you are applying for homestead for the first time. If a lender escrows your tax, ask the lender before you pay anything yourself so the bill is not paid twice.

Ask staff to explain the county and school lines on your statement. They will also tell you whether the figure is current through the day you plan to close. A bill printed in October and a payoff needed in December can differ, and the closing agent will want the later number in writing.

Owners of hillside or valley acreage should also ask the assessors about preferential assessment, since that number goes through a separate desk and has its own paperwork. Questions about the grant or the senior exemptions are best settled by phone before you list, so a buyer's agent hears one consistent answer about what the next owner will pay.

faqs.q: When must Walker County real estate tax be paid?
faqs.a: Two months after the notices are mailed, usually December 20. If your bill shows another date, follow the bill.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about a Walker County tax bill?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner's staff at 706-638-2929, in either the Rock Spring or the Rossville office. Value questions go to the assessors at 706-638-4823.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Walker County valuation?
faqs.a: The 45th day after the notice's mailing date. The assessors look first, and a Board of Equalization hearing follows if you stay in dispute.

faqs.q: Where do I file for homestead exemption in Walker County?
faqs.a: At the Tax Commissioner's counter, with April 1 as the cutoff for a new filing. First-time owners take their warranty deed along.

faqs.q: Does a lingering tax balance block a Walker County sale?
faqs.a: No. The balance is paid at closing from your proceeds. Get the amount in writing, and ask about earlier years if a tenant lived in the house or an heir inherited it.
